name: Web design and build
description: Scoping, pricing tiers, delivery steps, QA checklist, handover.

cards.subject: A project brief
says: captures the client's goals, audience and constraints in one written document
gives everyone the same written starting point for the project
cards.use: need everyone to start from the same written goals
not: replaces the need for any later sign-off

cards.subject: A discovery workshop
says: gathers stakeholders to surface goals, users and risks before the work is scoped
turns vague assumptions into questions that can be answered
cards.use: do not yet know who the site's real users are
not: is held only after the design has been approved

cards.subject: A statement of work
says: lists the deliverables, timeline and price the supplier commits to
is the document that any later change request is measured against
cards.use: need to agree in writing exactly what will be delivered
not: describes the client's business goals instead of the supplier's deliverables

cards.subject: An out-of-scope list
says: names work that is deliberately not included in the quote
stops unstated expectations from turning into free extra work
cards.use: hear a client assume that something is included
not: lists the features the client has already paid for

cards.subject: An assumptions log
says: records what the estimate relies on being true, such as content arriving on time
lets a broken assumption justify a re-estimate
cards.use: base an estimate on content the client has promised to supply
not: lists the features that are excluded from the quote

cards.subject: An acceptance criterion
says: states a testable condition that decides whether a deliverable is done
turns sign-off into a check against a list instead of an opinion
cards.use: need a deliverable to be signed off without argument
not: describes how the page should feel to visitors in general terms

cards.subject: A change request
says: records a new or altered requirement together with its effect on time and cost
must be approved before the extra work starts
cards.use: hear the client ask for a feature outside the agreed scope
not: is only needed when the client is unhappy with the quality of the work

cards.subject: A stakeholder map
says: identifies who decides, who advises and who is merely informed
exposes the person holding a veto before they appear late in the project
cards.use: suspect several people will give conflicting feedback
not: lists the visitors the finished site is meant to serve

cards.subject: A milestone payment schedule
says: ties parts of the fee to delivered stages of the project
limits the supplier's exposure if the client stalls after the first stage
cards.use: agree a fee for a project that runs over several months
not: charges the whole fee after the site has gone live

cards.subject: A success metric
says: defines how the client will judge the site after launch, such as enquiries or conversion rate
is agreed before design so design choices can be tested against it
cards.use: need to show later whether the redesign worked
not: is chosen after launch from whichever numbers look best

cards.subject: A single point of approval
says: names the one person who can give final client sign-off
stops feedback rounds from reopening decisions already settled
cards.use: see settled decisions overturned by a newly involved reviewer
not: removes the need to record approvals in writing

cards.subject: A page sitemap
says: lists every page of the site and shows how pages nest under each other
is drawn before wireframes so the structure can be agreed first
cards.use: need to agree what pages the site will have
not: is the XML file submitted to search engines

cards.subject: Information architecture
says: organises and labels content so visitors can predict where to find things
covers the structure, navigation and naming of the whole site
cards.use: find that visitors cannot locate content that exists
not: is the visual styling of the navigation bar

cards.subject: A user journey
says: traces the steps one type of visitor takes to reach a goal
shows where a visitor would hesitate or drop out
cards.use: need to design around the path from landing to enquiry
not: lists every page of the site in one hierarchy

cards.subject: A content inventory
says: lists the pages and assets on the existing site
lets the team mark each item to keep, rewrite, merge or delete
cards.use: start a redesign of a site that already has hundreds of pages
not: is a list of pages the new site will add

cards.subject: A content model
says: defines the types of content and the fields each type has
is settled before the CMS is configured so editors get sensible forms
cards.use: need to decide what fields an event or case study needs
not: is the diagram of the site's folder structure on the server

cards.subject: A page template
says: fixes the layout and regions shared by pages of one kind
lets editors add pages without redesigning each one
cards.use: expect dozens of pages that all look the same
not: defines which fields a content type stores

cards.subject: Card sorting
says: asks participants to group topic cards into categories they find natural
reveals how users expect content to be organised
cards.use: need evidence for how to group navigation items
not: asks participants to find a given item in a proposed menu

cards.subject: Tree testing
says: asks participants to find items in a text-only menu hierarchy
measures whether a proposed structure works before any design exists
cards.use: want to check a proposed menu structure with real people
not: asks participants to sort topic cards into groups they invent

cards.subject: A navigation label
says: works best when it uses the words visitors use
fails when it copies the client's internal department names
cards.use: see a menu filled with internal jargon
not: should be as clever and short as possible

cards.subject: A content migration plan
says: decides which existing content moves, is rewritten or is dropped
maps old pages to their new homes so redirects can be built
cards.use: must carry hundreds of existing pages onto a new platform
not: assumes all old pages can be copied across unchanged

cards.subject: A wireframe
says: shows layout and content priority without colour or final imagery
lets structure be discussed before visual design begins
cards.use: want feedback on layout before any visual styling
not: fixes the final colours and typography of the page

cards.subject: A style guide
says: records the colours, typefaces and usage rules for the brand on the web
keeps new pages consistent after the original designer has left
cards.use: expect other people to add pages later
not: lists every page of the site

cards.subject: A clickable prototype
says: links screens together so a flow can be tried without code
lets users and stakeholders test a journey before development
cards.use: need stakeholders to try a journey before build starts
not: shows static layout boxes with no interaction

cards.subject: A responsive breakpoint
says: is a screen width at which the layout changes
is chosen where the content starts to look wrong, not by device model
cards.use: need to agree how layouts adapt to narrower screens
not: is a fixed list of phone models the site supports

cards.subject: A design token
says: stores a design value such as a colour or spacing step under a name
lets one change to a value flow through every place it is used
cards.use: want a brand colour change to apply everywhere at once
not: is a license key that unlocks a font

cards.subject: A component library
says: collects reusable interface parts such as buttons, cards and forms
gives designers and developers the same parts to work from
cards.use: find buttons built three different ways across pages
not: stores the single values for colours and spacing

cards.subject: An annotated design spec
says: adds notes on behaviour, spacing and content rules to the visual design
answers what a flat picture cannot, such as what happens on hover or overflow
cards.use: hand a design to developers who were not in the design meetings
not: is a flat picture exported for the client to approve

cards.subject: An interface state
says: is a condition of a component such as hovered, focused, disabled, empty or in error
is missing from a design that shows only the ideal case
cards.use: find a design shows a form only in its tidy default state
not: are the different pages visitors can reach from the home page

cards.subject: Web font licensing
says: decides whether a typeface may be served on the web and from where
needs checking before design is approved because the font may not be allowed
cards.use: see the designer pick a commercial typeface for the client's site
not: is irrelevant once the font file is on the server

cards.subject: A design review
says: compares the built page with the approved design at each breakpoint
catches spacing, state and responsive differences before QA starts
cards.use: suspect the build has drifted from the approved design
not: asks the client whether they like the colour palette

cards.subject: A hand-off asset export
says: provides icons as SVG and photos at the sizes the layout needs
saves developers from guessing sizes and formats
cards.use: need developers to build from final graphics
not: gives developers only a link to the live competitor site

cards.subject: WordPress
says: lets editors manage pages and posts through a familiar admin screen
extends its behaviour through themes and plugins
suits brochure sites, blogs and shops with a quick timeline
cards.use: need a brochure site that editors can update themselves quickly
not: is the right choice for every site with complex business logic

cards.subject: Drupal
says: models content as nodes of defined content types with fields
offers taxonomy, Views and fine-grained roles for complex content
typically needs more developer skill to build and maintain
cards.use: face a content-heavy site with many content types and tight permissions
not: is a PHP framework with no content management features

cards.subject: Laravel
says: is a PHP framework for custom applications, not a CMS
gives full control over logic and data models
leaves admin and content features to be built or paired with a CMS
cards.use: need booking, portal or accounting logic that a CMS would fight
not: ships with a page editor and theme system like a CMS

cards.subject: A static site generator
says: builds plain HTML files from templates and content files at build time
needs no database or application server on the live site
suits sites whose content changes rarely
cards.use: want a very fast, low-maintenance site with little changing content
not: renders each page from a database on every request

cards.subject: A headless CMS
says: stores and edits content but leaves the front end to a separate application
serves content to the front end through an API
lets one content store feed a website and an app
cards.use: need the same content on a website and a mobile app
not: includes the themes that render the public pages

cards.subject: A page builder
says: lets editors assemble layouts visually inside the CMS
can give editors design freedom that breaks consistency
adds weight to the page when it outputs heavy markup
cards.use: want editors to lay out landing pages without a developer
not: guarantees every page will follow the style guide

cards.subject: A custom theme
says: is built for one site's design instead of reusing a ready-made look
gives control of markup and performance
carries the cost of being maintained by the supplier
cards.use: need a design that no purchased theme can match
not: is the quickest route to a launch on any budget

cards.subject: A child theme
says: inherits a parent theme and overrides only the parts you change
keeps your changes safe when the parent theme is updated
cards.use: want to adjust a purchased theme without losing changes on update
not: is a theme built from nothing for one client

cards.subject: A WordPress custom post type
says: adds a new kind of content such as events or case studies
gets its own admin menu and its own archive
cards.use: need to manage case studies separately from blog posts in WordPress
not: is a plugin that changes the site's colours

cards.subject: A Drupal content type
says: defines the fields and settings for one kind of node
is created in the admin or in exported configuration
cards.use: need to model events with date and venue fields in Drupal
not: is a stylesheet that restyles Drupal nodes

cards.subject: A Laravel migration
says: is a versioned PHP file that changes the database schema
can be run and rolled back with Artisan commands
cards.use: need to add a column to the database in a repeatable way
not: is a command that moves the site to a new server

cards.subject: Version control
says: records every change to the code with an author and message
allows a bad change to be found and reversed
cards.use: need to track and undo changes to a site's code
not: is the same as taking a nightly backup of the server

cards.subject: A staging environment
says: is a copy of the live site for testing changes before release
should match production in versions and configuration
cards.use: need to test an update before real visitors see it
not: is the place where clients upload their final content for visitors

cards.subject: A feature branch
says: isolates one piece of work from the main line
is merged only after review
cards.use: need to build a new section without disturbing the working site
not: is edited directly on the live server

cards.subject: An environment variable
says: keeps a secret or setting out of the code in the repository
differs between local, staging and production
cards.use: must keep an API key or database password out of the repository
not: is safe to commit as long as the repository is private

cards.subject: A code review
says: has a second person read a change before it is merged
finds defects and security slips a single author overlooks
cards.use: want a second pair of eyes on a change before release
not: replaces the need for any testing

cards.subject: A least-privilege editor role
says: gives an editor only the permissions needed for their tasks
reduces the damage a stolen or mistaken account can do
cards.use: hand an admin login to several client staff
not: gives every editor administrator rights for convenience

cards.subject: Plugin vetting
says: checks a plugin's maintenance, reviews and necessity before it is installed
limits the attack surface and conflicts a CMS site carries
cards.use: are asked to add a plugin for a small feature
not: installs any plugin with a high download count on the live site first

cards.subject: Form spam protection
says: keeps bots from flooding form submissions
can use a challenge, a hidden honeypot field or rate limiting
cards.use: find the contact form full of junk submissions
not: removes the need to validate input on the server

cards.subject: A pre-change backup
says: captures files and database before an update or release
is only useful if a restore from it has been proven
cards.use: are about to update a core system or run a release
not: can be skipped if the update worked on staging

cards.subject: A deployment script
says: performs release steps the same way every time
reduces the chance of a forgotten manual step
cards.use: find releases fail when different people upload files by hand
not: is written fresh by whoever is releasing each time

cards.subject: A broken link check
says: finds links that lead to missing pages
should include links in menus, footers and body content
cards.use: need to confirm no link on the site returns an error
not: tests whether forms deliver email

cards.subject: A proofreading pass
says: checks wording, names, numbers and contact details on the pages
is done on the built site, not only in the document copy
cards.use: want typos and wrong phone numbers caught before launch
not: checks that links open the right pages

cards.subject: A cross-browser test
says: checks that the site works in the browsers visitors use
finds differences in rendering and unsupported features
cards.use: need to confirm layouts hold in Safari as well as Chrome
not: measures how fast the site loads

cards.subject: A responsive test
says: checks layouts at phone, tablet and desktop widths
includes both portrait and landscape orientation
cards.use: need to confirm the layout adapts to narrow screens
not: compares rendering across different browser engines

cards.subject: A real-device test
says: uses actual phones and tablets rather than only a desktop emulator
finds touch, font and performance issues emulation hides
cards.use: want evidence that the site is usable on a real mid-range phone
not: is replaced entirely by resizing a desktop browser window

cards.subject: A form submission test
says: submits each form with valid and invalid data
confirms the confirmation page and the stored enquiry
cards.use: need to confirm an enquiry reaches the right inbox
not: tests only that the form is visible on the page

cards.subject: An email deliverability test
says: checks that notification mail arrives in the inbox, not spam
depends on SPF and DKIM records for the sending domain
cards.use: find that form notification emails go missing or land in spam
not: confirms that the form shows a thank-you message

cards.subject: A smoke test
says: checks the few critical paths work after a deploy
is quick, shallow and repeated at every release
cards.use: need a fast pass/fail check right after a release
not: exhaustively tests every feature with every data combination

cards.subject: A regression test
says: re-checks existing behaviour after a change
catches a fix that has broken something that worked before
cards.use: fear an update to one area has broken another
not: checks only the new feature that was just built

cards.subject: User acceptance testing
says: has the client or real users verify the site against agreed criteria
ends with a recorded sign-off
cards.use: need the client to confirm the build meets the acceptance criteria
not: is run by the developers on their own machines

cards.subject: A console error check
says: opens the browser developer tools and looks for errors on each template
reveals failed requests and script errors invisible to the eye
cards.use: suspect a script or resource fails silently
not: compares the page with the approved design

cards.subject: Largest Contentful Paint
says: measures when the biggest visible element has rendered
is considered good at 2.5 seconds or less
cards.use: find the hero image appears late
not: measures how quickly the page responds to a tap

cards.subject: Interaction to Next Paint
says: measures how quickly the page responds visually to user interactions
is considered good at 200 milliseconds or less
cards.use: find taps and clicks feel sluggish on a script-heavy page
not: measures when the largest element becomes visible

cards.subject: Cumulative Layout Shift
says: measures how much visible content moves unexpectedly
is considered good at 0.1 or less
cards.use: see text jump when an image or ad loads
not: measures server response speed

cards.subject: Time to First Byte
says: measures how long the server takes to begin answering a request
is improved by caching, a nearer server or faster back-end code
cards.use: suspect a slow server or slow database queries
not: measures how much the layout moves

cards.subject: Image compression
says: reduces file size by removing data the eye barely notices
is usually the largest single saving on a typical page
cards.use: find the page weight is dominated by photographs
not: changes the dimensions displayed on screen

cards.subject: A responsive image
says: lets the browser pick an image file sized for the screen
uses srcset and sizes attributes
cards.use: serve phones a smaller file than desktops
not: serves one large image and shrinks it using CSS alone

cards.subject: Lazy loading
says: delays loading images below the fold until the visitor scrolls near
should not be applied to the hero image that appears first
cards.use: have a long page with many images far down
not: loads every image before the page is shown

cards.subject: Browser caching
says: lets repeat visitors reuse files they already downloaded
is controlled by response headers such as Cache-Control
cards.use: want returning visitors not to download unchanged files again
not: speeds up only the very first visit to the site

cards.subject: Minification
says: removes whitespace and comments from CSS and JavaScript files
reduces transfer size without changing behaviour
cards.use: want smaller script and style files with the same behaviour
not: rewrites images into a lighter format

cards.subject: A render-blocking resource
says: stops the browser painting until it has been downloaded and processed
is typically a stylesheet or script in the head without defer
cards.use: find the page stays blank while scripts download
not: is an image that loads after the page is visible

cards.subject: A CDN
says: serves static files from servers close to the visitor
reduces load on the origin server
cards.use: have visitors in several countries far from the server
not: stores a copy of the database for editors

cards.subject: A performance budget
says: sets limits such as page weight or load time that a build must stay within
makes a regression visible during development instead of after launch
cards.use: fear that added features will slowly bloat the site
not: is the money set aside for server hosting

cards.subject: Field data
says: comes from real visitors' browsers over time
can differ from a one-off lab test on a fast connection
cards.use: find a lab score looks fine but visitors complain of slowness
not: comes from a single synthetic test under controlled settings

cards.subject: WCAG
says: is the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines published by the W3C
organises requirements under the principles perceivable, operable, understandable and robust
cards.use: need the standard that accessibility requirements are measured against
not: is a law that applies in only one country

cards.subject: Alternative text
says: describes the purpose of an image for people who cannot see it
is left empty for purely decorative images
cards.use: add an image that carries information
not: should be stuffed with keywords for search engines

cards.subject: Colour contrast
says: needs at least 4.5 to 1 for normal text at WCAG level AA
is checked with a contrast tool, not by eye
cards.use: choose text and background colours for body copy
not: is satisfied by any dark text on a coloured background

cards.subject: Keyboard navigation
says: means every function can be used without a mouse
follows a tab order that matches the visual order
cards.use: need the menu and forms to work for someone who cannot use a mouse
not: is only required on mobile devices

cards.subject: A focus indicator
says: shows which element currently has keyboard focus
must not be removed unless replaced with a visible alternative
cards.use: find a stylesheet that sets outline to none on links
not: highlights the element under the mouse pointer

cards.subject: A semantic heading
says: structures a page as a nested outline from h1 downward
lets screen reader users jump between sections
cards.use: need a page that can be navigated by headings
not: is chosen by font size rather than by level

cards.subject: A form label
says: is programmatically associated with its input
remains visible when the placeholder text disappears
cards.use: build a form field that a screen reader must announce correctly
not: is satisfied by placeholder text alone

cards.subject: ARIA
says: adds roles and states that assistive technology reads
should be used only when no native HTML element does the job
cards.use: are tempted to add roles to a div acting as a button
not: makes a non-interactive element keyboard operable on its own

cards.subject: A skip link
says: lets keyboard users jump past repeated navigation to the main content
is often hidden until it receives focus
cards.use: have a long menu before the main content on every page
not: makes the menu collapse on small screens

cards.subject: A video caption
says: gives access to spoken content for people who cannot hear it
also helps people in noisy places or without sound
cards.use: publish a video with speech
not: is only needed for live video

cards.subject: Screen reader testing
says: checks what assistive technology announces in practice
finds problems automated scanners cannot detect
cards.use: want to confirm a modal or menu is usable without sight
not: is fully replaced by running an automated checker

cards.subject: Reduced motion
says: is a user setting the CSS can respect through a media query
protects people for whom animation causes discomfort
cards.use: include parallax or large animations on pages
not: is ignored because animation is purely decorative

cards.subject: A title tag
says: names the page in search results and browser tabs
should be unique for each page
cards.use: need each page to have a distinct label in search results
not: is the visible h1 heading on the page

cards.subject: A meta description
says: summarises the page as a snippet under the title in results
does not directly set the ranking but affects whether people click
cards.use: want to control the summary shown under the page title
not: is displayed as the page's heading on the site

cards.subject: An XML sitemap
says: lists the URLs a site wants search engines to find
is submitted through tools such as Search Console
cards.use: want search engines to discover every important page
not: is the page that visitors use to browse the site

cards.subject: A robots.txt file
says: tells crawlers which paths they may not crawl
does not secure a page, since the file itself is public
cards.use: need to keep crawlers out of a utility path
not: reliably removes a page that is already indexed

cards.subject: A 301 redirect
says: tells browsers and crawlers a page has moved permanently
passes visitors and ranking signals to the new address
cards.use: retire an old URL that has links and traffic
not: tells crawlers the move is only temporary

cards.subject: A redirect map
says: pairs each old URL with its new destination before launch
is built from the content inventory and analytics
cards.use: launch a redesign that changes many URLs
not: is created after launch from the 404 errors that appear

cards.subject: A canonical tag
says: names the preferred URL among duplicates
consolidates signals from near-identical pages
cards.use: serve the same content under several URLs
not: blocks the page from appearing in search

cards.subject: A noindex directive
says: asks search engines to leave a page out of their index
only works if the crawler is allowed to fetch the page
cards.use: need to keep a staging site out of search results
not: blocks crawling of the page in robots.txt

cards.subject: Google Search Console
says: reports how the search engine crawls and indexes a verified site
accepts a sitemap and shows indexing errors
cards.use: want to see which pages are indexed and which are not
not: measures what visitors do on the site after arriving

cards.subject: Web analytics
says: measures visits and behaviour on the site
must be installed and checked before launch to avoid a data gap
cards.use: need to count visits and conversions after launch
not: reports which pages the search engine has crawled

cards.subject: Structured data
says: describes page content to search engines in a defined vocabulary
is commonly added as JSON-LD
cards.use: want a business, article or FAQ to be understood in a machine-readable way
not: is a visible text block placed at the bottom of the page

cards.subject: Open Graph tags
says: control the title, description and image shown when a link is shared
are read by social and chat platforms, not used to rank pages
cards.use: want a shared link to show the right image and title
not: control the snippet shown in search results

cards.subject: Host and protocol consolidation
says: redirects www, non-www, http and https variants to one canonical form
prevents the same page being indexed at several addresses
cards.use: find the site loads at both http and https and with and without www
not: adds a canonical tag only to the home page

cards.subject: A go-live checklist
says: lists the steps to be done before, during and after switching the site live
has each step assigned to a named person
cards.use: need the launch to be a routine, not an improvisation
not: is written the evening of the launch

cards.subject: A content freeze
says: stops edits to the old and new sites for a short period
prevents content being lost in the switch
cards.use: are about to copy content and cut over to the new site
not: lets everyone keep editing both sites during the cutover

cards.subject: A DNS cutover
says: points the domain at the new server
takes time to reach visitors because resolvers cache records
cards.use: need visitors to be sent to the new hosting
not: moves the site files to the server

cards.subject: A lowered TTL
says: shortens how long resolvers cache a DNS record
is set a day or more before the cutover
cards.use: want a DNS change to take effect and be reversible quickly
not: is changed only after the cutover is done

cards.subject: An SSL certificate
says: lets the site be served over HTTPS
must be installed and tested with redirects before launch
cards.use: need the site to serve over a secure connection
not: is not required if the site has no login

cards.subject: A rollback plan
says: defines how to return to the previous working state
states in advance who decides to use it and what triggers it
cards.use: must be able to recover if the launch goes badly
not: is written only after something goes wrong

cards.subject: A post-launch monitoring window
says: watches errors, forms and key pages closely in the first days
catches issues that testing on staging missed
cards.use: just switched a site live
not: ends the moment the DNS change is made

cards.subject: A forgotten noindex
says: is a leftover setting from staging that tells search engines to ignore the live site
is found by checking the live page source and robots rules after launch
cards.use: want to rule out the cause of a launched site vanishing from search
not: is harmless once the site has gone live

cards.subject: Email record preservation
says: keeps MX and related records intact when DNS is moved
stops company email from failing after a cutover
cards.use: move DNS to a new host for a domain that also receives email
not: is unnecessary because DNS covers only websites

cards.subject: A hard-coded URL
says: is a full address left in content or code that points at staging or the old site
survives a migration unless it is searched for and replaced
cards.use: find the live site still links to the staging address
not: is always updated automatically by the CMS

cards.subject: A soft launch
says: releases the site to a limited audience before the public announcement
exposes real-world issues while the impact is small
cards.use: fear untested real-world traffic will expose faults
not: is announced to the entire mailing list at once

cards.subject: A handover pack
says: collects documentation, logins, and process notes in one package
is delivered at the end of the project
cards.use: are about to close the project and pass the site to the client
not: contains only the invoice for the final payment

cards.subject: Admin training
says: shows editors how to update content, users and media
is recorded so new staff can learn from it later
cards.use: hand a CMS to a team who have never used it
not: is skipped when the CMS has a friendly interface

cards.subject: An editor guide
says: documents routine tasks in the client's own terms
answers questions before they become support requests
cards.use: want clients to manage routine edits without calling the supplier
not: describes how to modify the theme code

cards.subject: Credentials transfer
says: hands over ownership of admin accounts, hosting and domain logins through a secure route
ends with the supplier's own temporary access being removed
cards.use: finish the project and must pass over the keys
not: sends all passwords in one plain email

cards.subject: Domain and hosting ownership
says: should sit in an account the client controls
avoids the client being locked out if the supplier relationship ends
cards.use: set up accounts at the start of a project
not: is kept in the supplier's name by default

cards.subject: A warranty period
says: covers fixes to defects in the delivered work for an agreed time
excludes new features and issues caused by later changes
cards.use: agree what support follows launch at no extra charge
not: covers any request the client makes after launch

cards.subject: A maintenance plan
says: covers updates, backups, monitoring and fixes on an ongoing basis
is part of the quote, not an optional extra for a CMS site
cards.use: need someone to own CMS and plugin patching
not: ends when the warranty period begins

cards.subject: A post-launch review
says: compares results with the success metrics agreed at the start
records lessons for the next project
cards.use: want to learn what worked after a few weeks live
not: is held before launch to approve the design

cards.subject: A support boundary
says: states what is covered by the plan and what is chargeable
prevents a misunderstanding about who fixes a plugin conflict
cards.use: are asked to fix something that the client's own edit broke
not: promises that every request will be handled at no extra cost

cards.subject: A restore test
says: proves that a backup can actually rebuild the site
is run before handover, not left until an incident
cards.use: trust a backup that has never been restored
not: confirms a backup file exists on the server

cards.subject: Update ownership
says: names who applies CMS and plugin updates after launch
leaves a site exposed to published vulnerabilities if nobody holds it
cards.use: hand over a CMS site to a client with no technical staff
not: is automatic with every CMS and needs no owner

cards.subject: The pricing master switch
says: is GG_PRICING_LIVE in gg-sales-config.php
keeps published prices off the GGLink site until they are real
cards.use: must stop unfinished prices from being shown to visitors
not: is edited by visitors through the contact form

cards.subject: The results master switch
says: is GG_RESULTS_LIVE in gg-sales-config.php
keeps client results off the GGLink site until they are real and evidenced
cards.use: need to hold back outcome figures that cannot be proven
not: publishes testimonials before they have been checked

cards.subject: The cost-level scale
says: runs through free, semi-free, paid, custom and enterprise in Moksy's early solution notes
sits beside solution families such as WordPress-based, Drupal-based and Laravel-based
cards.use: want to classify a candidate solution by cost level
not: is a fixed price list published on the GGLink site

cards.subject: The GGLink technologies strip
says: shows WordPress, Drupal, CodeIgniter, Cloudflare and cPanel among the technologies GGLink works with
is a capability showing, not a case study
cards.use: need to know which platforms the GGLink site presents as its own
not: lists the stack that runs gglearn, ggsocial and ggmoney

cards.subject: The deploy check script
says: is php deploy-check.php, run before and after uploading the GGLink site
only reports and changes nothing
exits non-zero if something would break the site
cards.use: need to verify a GGLink release before and after upload
not: rewrites the site's files to fix problems it finds

cards.subject: The GGLink database exposure check
says: requests /storage/gglink.sqlite and expects 403 or 404
signals that .htaccess is not being honoured if the file downloads
cards.use: finish a GGLink deploy and must check content is not downloadable
not: confirms that the contact form emails arrive

cards.subject: The GGLink contact form check
says: is a post-deploy test where the form lands on the thank-you page
expects the enquiry to appear in the admin and the notification email to arrive
cards.use: need to prove the GGLink enquiry flow works after a deploy
not: checks the sitemap is valid XML

cards.subject: The GGLink robots.txt
says: allows crawlers and blocks /cgi-bin/, /vendor/ and /thank-you.php
points to the sitemap at www.gglink.co.uk/sitemap.xml
cards.use: need to see what the GGLink site tells crawlers
not: disallows the whole site for crawlers other than Google

cards.subject: The duplicate wildcard robots.txt bug
says: was a second User-agent: * group with Disallow: / in the previous GGLink robots.txt
merged into the wildcard group and blocked non-Google crawlers such as Bing
cards.use: suspect a robots.txt blocks only some crawlers
not: was caused by a missing sitemap line

cards.subject: The GGLink blog feed
says: is read from the WordPress REST API through BLOG_API_URL
uses a 3-second timeout and a 900-second cache of the last good response
stops a slow blog from blocking a page render
cards.use: need to understand why a WordPress outage does not stop GGLink pages
not: fetches the blog without any timeout on each page

cards.subject: The GGLink first-run setup
says: asks for the first admin account at /admin/ and then closes that page
keeps Pricing, Credentials and Results hidden until real values exist
cards.use: launch a fresh GGLink deploy for the first time
not: ships with a default admin password to change later

cards.subject: SendGrid domain verification
says: is done for the whole gglink.co.uk domain, not a single sender
sets up SPF and DKIM to keep enquiry notifications out of spam
cards.use: need enquiry notification mail to be trusted by receiving servers
not: needs only a single verified address and no DNS changes

cards.subject: The GGLink secrets file
says: is config.local.php, which is gitignored and must not be committed
is created from config.local.php.example
cards.use: need to configure keys such as SENDGRID_API_KEY on a deploy
not: is committed to the repository so every deploy has the keys

cards.subject: The maintenance-in-the-quote rule
says: treats CMS maintenance as part of the quote, not an optional extra
exists because a CMS client site adds a second patch stream
cards.use: price a WordPress or Drupal client build
not: states a fixed maintenance fee from the GGLink price list

qa.q: What is the purpose of a page sitemap drawn during scoping?
qa.right: To agree which pages the site will have and how they nest before design starts
wrong: To tell search engines which URLs to crawl after launch
To record the colours and fonts used on each page
To list the plugins that will be installed on the server
qa.why: A page sitemap is a planning document; the XML sitemap is a separate file for search engines.

qa.q: A client asks for an extra booking feature halfway through the build. What is the right first step?
qa.right: Record it as a change request with its effect on time and cost, and get approval before starting
wrong: Build it quietly and mention it on the final invoice
Refuse it because the scope can never change
Add it to the live site first and agree the price afterwards
qa.why: Work outside the agreed scope is handled through an approved change request.

qa.q: Which of these belongs in alternative text for an image that is only decoration?
qa.right: Nothing: the alt attribute is left empty
wrong: A description of every colour in the image
The keywords the page wants to rank for
The file name of the image
qa.why: An empty alt tells screen readers to skip a purely decorative image.

qa.q: Why is a staging site used?
qa.right: To test changes on a copy of the live site before visitors see them
wrong: To store the final backups of the live site
To host the site permanently for lower cost
To let search engines index the new design early
qa.why: Staging is a pre-production copy for safe testing.

qa.q: What does a 301 status code tell a browser?
qa.right: The page has moved permanently to a new address
wrong: The page has been temporarily taken offline
The page does not exist and never did
The request needs a login before the page is shown
qa.why: 301 means moved permanently; a 302 is temporary.

qa.q: Which file lists the URLs you want search engines to discover?
qa.right: An XML sitemap
wrong: The robots.txt allow rules alone
The favicon file
The .htaccess file
qa.why: An XML sitemap lists URLs; robots.txt can point to it with a Sitemap line.

qa.q: A client's team gives conflicting feedback every round. Which scoping artefact would have prevented this?
qa.right: A single point of approval who gives final sign-off
wrong: A longer out-of-scope list
A more detailed colour palette
A faster hosting plan
qa.why: Naming one decision maker stops decided matters being reopened by each new reviewer.

qa.q: Which statement about WordPress and Drupal is the best summary for a client choosing between them?
qa.right: WordPress suits familiar editing and quick brochure sites; Drupal suits complex structured content and fine-grained permissions
wrong: Drupal is always cheaper to build because it needs less developer skill
WordPress cannot be extended with plugins
Both are static site generators that need no database
qa.why: The choice depends on content complexity, editors, maintainer and budget.

qa.q: A project needs bespoke booking logic and an accounts area. Which choice is the most natural starting point?
qa.right: Laravel, because it is a framework for custom application logic
wrong: A hosted site builder, because it can be customised without limit
A static site generator, because it stores bookings in HTML
A WordPress child theme, because it contains the booking rules
qa.why: Laravel is a PHP application framework; CMSs are better for mostly content sites.

qa.q: What does this robots.txt do?
qa.right: Stops crawlers fetching anything under /private/ and points to the sitemap
wrong: Removes /private/ from search results immediately
Password-protects the /private/ folder
Blocks the whole site from all crawlers
qa.why: robots.txt asks crawlers not to fetch; it does not secure or de-index a path, and the file is public.

qa.q: A designer hands over only flat page pictures. What are developers most likely to miss?
qa.right: Hover, focus, error and empty states and responsive behaviour
wrong: The brand name
The size of the company's office
The address of the hosting provider
qa.why: A flat picture cannot show behaviour; annotated specs and state designs can.

qa.q: What is the main advantage of a content freeze before launch?
qa.right: Edits are not lost when content is copied and the site is switched
wrong: It makes the site load faster
It lets search engines index the site sooner
It removes the need for a rollback plan
qa.why: A freeze prevents changes being made to the old site after the copy.

qa.q: Which check confirms that a form notification actually reaches the client?
qa.right: Submit the form and confirm the email arrives in the inbox and the enquiry is stored
wrong: View the form on a phone and confirm it fits the screen
Run a spelling check on the form labels
Confirm the form has a placeholder in each field
qa.why: A form test follows the whole path from submission to the stored enquiry and mail.

qa.q: What does a good acceptance criterion look like?
qa.right: "The contact form shows a confirmation page and the enquiry appears in the admin"
wrong: "The site feels modern and friendly"
"The site is generally good"
"The client is happy"
qa.why: It is testable: anyone can check it and get the same answer.

qa.q: Why should the hero image not use lazy loading?
qa.right: It is visible straight away and lazy loading would delay the largest element
wrong: Lazy loading cannot be applied to JPEG files
Lazy loading blocks the keyboard
Hero images are never optimised
qa.why: Lazy loading is for below-the-fold images; delaying the visible one hurts Largest Contentful Paint.

qa.q: Which attribute pair lets the browser pick an image size for the screen?
qa.right: srcset and sizes
wrong: alt and title
rel and href
lang and dir
qa.why: srcset lists candidate files and sizes describes the displayed width.

qa.q: What do width and height attributes on an image help prevent?
qa.right: Layout shift while the image loads
wrong: Slow server responses
Broken links
Mixed content warnings
qa.why: They let the browser reserve space, which keeps Cumulative Layout Shift low.

qa.q: A client wants to launch a redesign that changes most URLs. What should be prepared before launch?
qa.right: A redirect map pairing each old URL with its new address
wrong: A list of keywords for the footer
A new logo in several sizes
A second domain name
qa.why: Without 301 redirects, visitors and ranking signals are lost on the old URLs.

qa.q: Which tag tells search engines which of several duplicate URLs is preferred?
qa.right: A canonical link element
wrong: A meta viewport tag
A title tag
An Open Graph image tag
qa.why: rel=canonical consolidates duplicates onto one preferred URL.

qa.q: A site has just launched and vanished from search. The page source holds the line below. What is the likely cause?
qa.right: A noindex setting left over from staging
wrong: The title tag is too long
The page has no canonical tag
The sitemap is in the wrong folder
qa.why: Staging is often set to noindex; it must be removed at go-live.

qa.q: Why does a team lower the DNS TTL a day before cutover?
qa.right: So the change reaches visitors quickly and can be reversed quickly
wrong: So the new server needs less memory
So the SSL certificate is issued earlier
So search engines can index the site early
qa.why: A short TTL makes resolvers re-check the record soon.

qa.q: Which Laravel Artisan command runs outstanding database migrations?
qa.right: php artisan migrate
wrong: php artisan db:run
php artisan schema:apply
php artisan update:tables
qa.why: migrate applies pending migrations; migrate:rollback reverses the last batch.

qa.q: Where should a database password for a client build live?
qa.right: In an environment variable or untracked config file outside the repository
wrong: In the theme file so every developer can see it
In a comment at the top of the home page template
In the page footer text
qa.why: Secrets stay out of version control and differ per environment.

qa.q: A WordPress site has 40 plugins and updates keep breaking pages. What is the best response?
qa.right: Audit the plugins, remove the unneeded ones and test updates on staging first
wrong: Disable updates so nothing changes
Add more plugins to fix the conflicts
Move the site to a larger server
qa.why: Plugin sprawl increases conflicts and attack surface.

qa.q: Which is the best test of a backup?
qa.right: Restore it to a clean environment and check the site works
wrong: Check the file size looks reasonable
Confirm the backup job's email said success
Download it and open it in a text editor
qa.why: A backup is proven only by a successful restore.

qa.q: A form's inputs use only placeholder text. What is the accessibility problem?
qa.right: The placeholder disappears and is not a reliable label for assistive technology
wrong: Placeholders cannot hold more than ten characters
The browser refuses to submit such forms
Placeholders only work on mobile devices
qa.why: Each input needs an associated, visible label element.

qa.q: Normal body text has a colour contrast of 3 to 1. Does it meet WCAG AA?
qa.right: No, normal text needs at least 4.5 to 1
wrong: Yes, any ratio above 2 to 1 passes
Yes, because the text is dark
No, it needs at least 21 to 1
qa.why: AA requires 4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 for large text.

qa.q: Which Core Web Vital reflects visible content jumping around while the page loads?
qa.right: Cumulative Layout Shift
wrong: Largest Contentful Paint
Time to First Byte
Interaction to Next Paint
qa.why: CLS scores unexpected layout movement, good at 0.1 or less.

qa.q: A client has not supplied content by the agreed date. What protects the supplier?
qa.right: An entry in the assumptions log that the estimate relied on timely content
wrong: The out-of-scope list
The site's robots.txt
A warranty period
qa.why: A broken assumption justifies a revised timeline or estimate.

qa.q: What distinguishes a smoke test from a regression test?
qa.right: A smoke test is a quick check of critical paths; a regression test re-checks existing behaviour more broadly
wrong: A smoke test checks colour; a regression test checks fonts
A smoke test runs only on live sites; a regression test only on staging
They are two names for the same test
qa.why: Smoke tests are fast and shallow; regression tests look for breakage in things that worked.

qa.q: A mobile visitor taps a menu and nothing happens for a noticeable moment. Which metric points at this?
qa.right: Interaction to Next Paint
wrong: Largest Contentful Paint
Cumulative Layout Shift
DNS lookup time
qa.why: INP measures responsiveness to interactions; good is 200 ms or less.

qa.q: A designer chooses a commercial typeface for the client's site. What should be checked before sign-off?
qa.right: Whether the licence allows web use and how the font files will be served
wrong: Whether the typeface name is in the client's logo
Whether the font appears in the browser's default list
Nothing, because fonts are free to embed
qa.why: Desktop licences often exclude web embedding.

qa.q: A team asks whether to use ARIA roles to make a clickable div act as a button. What is the best advice?
qa.right: Use a native button element, because it is keyboard operable and announced correctly by default
wrong: Add role=button and nothing else, because that is enough
Add tabindex only and skip the role
Use a link with no href
qa.why: The first rule of ARIA is to use native HTML where it exists.

qa.q: Lab tests show a good score, but real visitors on slow phones complain. What is the best next step?
qa.right: Look at field data from real users and test on throttled mid-range devices
wrong: Ignore complaints because the lab score is passing
Delete the analytics script
Increase image sizes for sharper results
qa.why: Field data reflects real conditions that a single lab run can hide.

qa.q: A site is reachable at four addresses (http/https, www/non-www) and all are indexed. What should be done?
qa.right: Redirect all variants to one canonical address with 301s and confirm one canonical form
wrong: Add a noindex to the home page only
Block all four addresses in robots.txt
Create a second sitemap for each variant
qa.why: Consolidation prevents duplicate indexing and split signals.

qa.q: Why is maintenance included in a CMS site quote?
qa.right: A CMS adds a second patch stream, and someone must own updates, backups and monitoring
wrong: Because clients like paying monthly
Because CMS sites never need updates
Because maintenance replaces the warranty period
qa.why: Published vulnerabilities in CMS software are actively scanned for.

qa.q: A client edits a plugin setting after handover and the site breaks. The plan is silent on this. What would have avoided the dispute?
qa.right: A written support boundary stating what is covered and what is chargeable
wrong: A longer warranty on the design
A faster server
An additional sitemap
qa.why: A support boundary sets expectations before an issue appears.

qa.q: The live site emails stopped working after DNS moved to the new host. What was likely missed?
qa.right: The MX and related mail records were not recreated
wrong: The title tags were duplicated
The canonical tag pointed to staging
The image sizes were too large
qa.why: Moving DNS means the existing mail records must be preserved.

qa.q: Which QA gap lets a launched site still link to the staging address?
qa.right: A search for hard-coded URLs in content and code was not done
wrong: A responsive test at tablet width
A spelling check of headings
A colour contrast check
qa.why: Absolute URLs stay unchanged on migration unless replaced.

qa.q: A site has many content types with taxonomies, workflow and multiple languages. Which fit is the best starting point?
qa.right: Drupal, because its content modelling, roles and multilingual features suit complex content
wrong: A hosted site builder, because it is always the cheapest
A static page with all content in one HTML file
Laravel with no CMS, because forms are enough
qa.why: Drupal's strengths are structured content and fine-grained permissions, at higher build cost.

qa.q: How should success be measured after a redesign?
qa.right: Against the success metrics agreed before design, such as enquiries or conversion rate
wrong: Against whichever statistics look best after launch
By how many pages were created
By how long the project took
qa.why: Metrics agreed up front stop the post-launch review turning into opinion.

qa.q: A client team finds the rollback plan unnecessary because "the cutover is only a DNS change." What is the strongest reason to keep it?
qa.right: The cutover can still fail in ways testing missed, and a decision and trigger agreed in advance saves time under pressure
wrong: Rollback plans are required for the SSL certificate to work
It prevents DNS from caching old records
It replaces the need for post-launch monitoring
qa.why: A rollback plan names who decides and what triggers it before stress arrives.

qa.q: A developer proposes blocking the old site in robots.txt to remove it from search. Why is that unreliable?
qa.right: Blocked URLs can remain indexed from links, and the crawler cannot see a noindex on a page it may not fetch
wrong: robots.txt is ignored by all crawlers
robots.txt can only block images
It deletes the pages from the server
qa.why: To de-index, allow crawling and serve noindex or return 404 or 410.

qa.q: A new build scores well in the lab, yet LCP is poor for real users in one country. What should be investigated first?
qa.right: The CDN and TTFB for visitors in that region, and the LCP element's loading
wrong: The meta description length
The colour contrast of the footer
The number of Open Graph tags
qa.why: Regional distance and server response often explain field-only problems.

qa.q: A client asks you to guarantee the new site will rank first for a key phrase. What is the best reply?
qa.right: Explain that ranking depends on factors outside delivery, and commit instead to launch SEO basics and agreed metrics
wrong: Guarantee it and include it in the contract
Refuse to discuss SEO at all
Buy links to meet the promise
qa.why: Delivery can control technical basics, not search rankings.

qa.q: A site passes an automated accessibility scan but a keyboard user cannot open the menu. What does this show?
qa.right: Automated scans find only some problems, so manual keyboard and screen reader testing are needed
wrong: The scan result must be wrong and should be discarded
Keyboard navigation is not part of WCAG
Only mobile users need a keyboard-operable menu
qa.why: Automated tools catch a minority of issues; interaction testing finds the rest.

qa.q: You are handing a site to a client who has no technical staff, and nobody will apply updates. What is the best decision?
qa.right: Agree a maintenance plan or name the party who owns updates, backups and monitoring, in writing
wrong: Hand over silently since the site works today
Disable the admin area
Give the client the supplier's own admin password
qa.why: An unowned CMS becomes vulnerable as fixes are published.

qa.q: Which command do GGLink deployments run before and after uploading?
qa.right: php deploy-check.php
wrong: npm run deploy
composer install
php artisan migrate
qa.why: deploy-check.php reports problems and changes nothing; it exits non-zero if something would break the site.

qa.q: After a GGLink deploy, https://www.gglink.co.uk/storage/gglink.sqlite downloads. What does that mean?
qa.right: The .htaccess rules are not being honoured and must be fixed before going live
wrong: The database backup succeeded
The site is cached by a CDN
Nothing, because the file is public by design
qa.why: The database must return 403 or 404.

qa.q: Which pair of switches keeps pricing and results hidden on the GGLink site until they are real?
qa.right: GG_PRICING_LIVE and GG_RESULTS_LIVE
wrong: GG_DEBUG and GG_CACHE
SENDGRID_FROM and ENQUIRY_TO
RECAPTCHA_SECRET and BLOG_API_URL
qa.why: They are in gg-sales-config.php and gate claims that could be held against the company.

qa.q: How does the GGLink site avoid being slowed by its WordPress blog?
qa.right: It reads the REST API with a 3-second timeout and caches the last good response for 900 seconds
wrong: It fetches the blog only at midnight
It copies the whole WordPress database nightly
It waits for the blog with no limit
qa.why: A slow blog never blocks a page render.

qa.q: Where do the secrets for a GGLink deploy belong?
qa.right: In config.local.php, which is gitignored and created from the example file
wrong: In config.php committed to git
In the page footer
In the sitemap
qa.why: The settings include SENDGRID_API_KEY and RECAPTCHA_SECRET and must never be committed.

qa.q: A robots.txt contains two User-agent: * groups, the second with Disallow: /. What is the effect?
qa.right: They merge into one wildcard group and block every crawler that is not Google-specific
wrong: Only the second group is read
The sitemap line is ignored but crawlers are allowed
Crawlers receive a 404
qa.why: This was the bug fixed in the GGLink robots.txt, which had blocked Bing and DuckDuckGo.

qa.q: A GGLink enquiry email is not arriving. Which setup choice protects notifications from spam filters?
qa.right: Verify the whole gglink.co.uk domain in SendGrid so SPF and DKIM are set up
wrong: Verify only a personal inbox
Disable reCAPTCHA
Use a longer subject line
qa.why: Domain verification sets up SPF and DKIM; SENDGRID_FROM must also be a verified sender.

qa.q: A colleague wants to put a price list on the GGLink site "just as a draft" with GG_PRICING_LIVE on. What should you tell them?
qa.right: Keep it off until the figures are real, because published prices are claims the company can be held to
wrong: Turn it on because drafts are harmless
Add the prices only to the footer
Publish them and correct later
qa.why: The switch exists so unfinished or invented figures never reach visitors.
